rows.grounds: topic of daily worship for remaining conduct

items.question: Which topics concerning daily worship, the liṅga, and the rosary are to be explained?
premises: The purpose of remaining conduct is to be stated.
Daily worship on the altar is treated as supreme.
The nature of the liṅga and the rosary are explained in many ways.
items.inference: The text announces a cluster of topics on remaining conduct, daily altar worship, the liṅga, and the rosary.
uncertainties: The exact scope of śeṣavṛtti in this context is not fully specified.
items.plain_english: The purpose of the remaining conduct, daily worship, the supreme worship on the altar, the nature of the liṅga in its many forms, and the explanation of the rosary are to be set forth.

items.question: What topics are to be stated in the section on liṅga worship and occasional rites?
premises: The divisions of worship are to be stated.
These are presented in the revelation of liṅga worship.
The division, purpose, and procedure of occasional rites follow.
items.inference: The exposition moves from liṅga worship and its divisions to the classification and procedure of occasional rites.
uncertainties: Whether liṅgārcāsaṃprakāśane names a specific chapter or a general topic is unclear.
items.plain_english: The divisions of worship are to be explained in the revelation of liṅga worship, and then the division, purpose, and procedure of occasional rites.

rows.grounds: topics of festivals and circle worship

items.question: Which festival and special-day worship topics are to be explained next?
premises: The divisions of festivals and their specifics are to be treated.
Circle worship and its worship procedure are included.
The purpose of worship on guru days and other special days is explained.
items.inference: The text outlines a sequence covering festivals, circle worship, and worship on designated special days.
uncertainties: The exact range of days meant by ādyanta-dina is not fully explicit.
items.plain_english: The divisions of festivals, their specifics, circle worship and its performance, and the purpose of worship on guru days and other special beginning and end days are to be explained.

items.question: What procedures concerning death, gatherings, teaching, and guru worship are to be described?
premises: The examination of signs of death is to be treated.
The procedure for gatherings of yoginīs and others is included.
Procedures for exposition, hearing, and guru worship are also stated.
items.inference: The text announces a set of practical and ritual procedures ranging from death signs to teaching and guru worship.
uncertainties: The precise nature of the yoginī gathering is not specified in this verse.
items.plain_english: The examination of death, the procedure for gatherings of yoginīs and others, the method of exposition, the method of hearing, and the procedure for guru worship are to be described.

items.question: What topics are established in the twenty-eighth chapter on occasional rites?
premises: The twenty-eighth chapter is called the revelation of occasional rites.
It sets forth the division of the qualified self.
It also sets forth the sequence of the lineage of siddhas and their consorts.
items.inference: The twenty-eighth chapter combines classification of practitioners with the ordered lineage of siddhas and their consorts.
uncertainties: The exact criteria for the division of the qualified self are not given here.
items.plain_english: In the twenty-eighth chapter, called the revelation of occasional rites, are established the division of the qualified practitioner and the sequence of the lineage of siddhas and their consorts.

items.question: Which topics are covered in the twenty-ninth chapter of the text?
premises: The chapter includes procedures of worship and of the messenger.
It includes the sequence of the secret upaniṣad.
It includes initiation, consecration, and awakening.
items.inference: The twenty-ninth chapter gathers ritual procedures, esoteric instruction, and culminates in initiation, consecration, and awakening.
uncertainties: The meaning of dautavidhi as 'procedure of the messenger' follows a common Tantric sense but is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: In the twenty-ninth chapter are the procedures of worship and of the messenger, the sequence of the secret upaniṣad, initiation, consecration, and awakening.
